sections.h2: Where do Lincoln County, WA owners deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Everything runs through the courthouse at 450 Logan Street in Davenport. The Lincoln County Treasurer collects tax at PO Box 370, Davenport, WA 99122, and answers at 509-725-5061. The Assessor, at PO Box 400, values the property and can be reached at 509-725-7011 or 509-596-1454, Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

The Assessor's page states the legal standard: property is valued at 100% of true and fair market value, and each property must be physically inspected at least once every six years. The Assessor may reappraise sooner and may lower values when the market falls. Disagreements go to the County Board of Equalization.

The Treasurer takes mailed payments, online payments and payments by phone at 866-898-2915.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Lincoln County's setting and market?
sections.html:
Lincoln County is a wide, thinly settled county on the Big Bend Plateau in eastern Washington, and its parcels are far apart. It sits on the Channeled Scablands at 1,500 to 2,500 feet above sea level. Summers are hot and dry, winters are cold, and rainfall ranges from about 8 inches in the west to about 20 inches in the northeast. Interstate 90, U.S. 2 and U.S. 395 cross the county.

Davenport is the county seat and the largest city. Harrington and Sprague are the other cities, and the towns are Almira, Creston, Odessa, Reardan and Wilbur. The county was created in November 1883 and is named for Abraham Lincoln. With about 2,310 square miles of land and 4.7 people per square mile, it is the fifth-least populous county in Washington.

Census QuickFacts give the housing picture:

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 11,982, up 10.1% from April 2020.
  • Housing units: 6,178, with an owner-occupied rate of 80.4%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024: $292,800.
  • Median gross rent: $883. Median household income: $71,512.
  • Residents aged 65 and over: 28.5%.
  • Building permits in 2025: 67.

sections.h2: When are Lincoln County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Lincoln County bills are due April 30 and October 31, and in 2026 the second half was due Monday, November 2. The county's treasurer page posts that date, and it has now passed. If you still owe the second half on a parcel, interest is running.

The rules come from RCW 84.56.020. Tax of $50 or more can be paid in halves, and smaller bills are due in full on April 30. A mailed payment with no readable postmark that arrives within three business days of a due date is not delinquent. The treasurer may also accept partial payments and payment agreements, and any payment on delinquent years goes to the oldest year first unless you ask otherwise.

sections.h2: What does a late payment cost in Lincoln County?
sections.html:
The state sets the rates, and they follow the type of property. For a home with four or fewer units, interest is nine percent a year, charged monthly, with no penalty. For other real property and personal property, interest is twelve percent a year, plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and an added 8% penalty on December 1 of the year the tax is due.

Two other provisions in the statute are worth knowing:

  • Delinquent owners must get a notice that names the statewide foreclosure hotline, and after two years the treasurer passes the owner's name and property address to a homeownership resource center.
  • An income-qualified owner who lives in the home can have interest and penalties waived shortly before the three-year point if the parcel is in a foreclosure action, once per property.

Call 509-725-5061 for a payoff statement for any parcel before you list it.

sections.h2: How does a Lincoln County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
You file a petition with the Board of Equalization clerk by July 1 or within 30 days of the date the change of value notice was mailed, whichever is later. That 30-day period matches the statutory default in RCW 84.40.038. The county's Board page suggests asking the Assessor to re-inspect the property first, and the Assessor's Office will help with the petition form.

The Board's job is to find the market value on January 1 of the assessment year. You must show the Assessor erred and that the value does not match the market. Good evidence is sales of comparable property and maps or photographs that support your number. Other properties' assessments, the percentage of an increase, hardship and the tax amount cannot be considered.

The timeline is short. All evidence must be received at least 21 working days before the hearing, the hearing notice usually goes out 22 days in advance, and the decision usually arrives within two weeks. Bring copies, since anything presented becomes part of the record and is not returned. The Board must side with the Assessor unless your evidence is clear and convincing.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and programs can Lincoln County owners use?
sections.html:
The Assessor administers the senior citizen and disabled persons exemption and the current use program. For the exemption, the county explains that the value of your residence is frozen for tax purposes and you become exempt from excess and special levies and possibly regular levies. It covers a primary residence and up to one acre, and a mobile home can qualify even on rented land.

You must meet an age or disability test and own the home by December 31 of the year before the tax is due. For example, a 2026 exemption required ownership by December 31, 2025. You must have lived in the home at least six months by that date, and a copy of any trust that holds the home goes to the Assessor. The county notes that new medical deductions and a standard deduction have been added, and state law raises the thresholds for taxes payable in 2027, so ask for the current income limit instead of relying on an old brochure. The county links a screening tool from the state assessors' association.

RCW 84.36.381 lets a claimant move the exemption to a replacement residence after selling, which matters if you plan to buy again in the county.

sections.h2: What excise tax applies when a Lincoln County home sells?
sections.html:
The seller pays the Washington real estate excise tax, and it is due on the date of sale, not the recording date. The deed, the affidavit and the payment go to the county treasurer where the property sits, which in this county is the Treasurer in Davenport. The Department of Revenue warns that if the tax goes unpaid it can create a lien on the property.

If the tax is not paid within one month of the date of sale, interest runs from the sale date, and the 2026 and 2027 rate is 6%. The state portion for sales beginning January 1, 2027 is 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000 and 3.0% above. Farm and timber land that stays classified pays a flat 1.28% state rate. The Department of Revenue page also notes that the local rate is added. Ask the Treasurer for the local rate that applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: What is the Lincoln County tax title auction?
sections.html:
When a parcel is offered at foreclosure and draws no bid, it goes to the county as tax title property, and the county later resells it. Lincoln County scheduled its foreclosure and tax title auction for November 20, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. in the courthouse lobby, 450 Logan Street, with registration at 9:00 a.m.

The county's notice lists a parcel in the Town of Odessa with a minimum bid of $1,600, and shows a Town of Wilbur parcel withdrawn. If you own a parcel with years of unpaid tax, call the Treasurer before it reaches this stage.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Lincoln County property tax?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer at 509-725-5061 about payments and due dates, and the Assessor at 509-725-7011 or 509-596-1454 about values and exemptions. Both offices are at 450 Logan Street in Davenport.

faqs.q: When was the second half due in Lincoln County in 2026?
faqs.a: It was due Monday, November 2, 2026. That date has passed, so unpaid second-half tax is delinquent and accrues interest each month.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal in Lincoln County?
faqs.a: File by July 1 or within 30 days of the mailing date on your change of value notice, whichever is later. Ask the Assessor to re-inspect first, because that can settle the question without a hearing.

faqs.q: What interest applies to a late Lincoln County residential bill?
faqs.a: A residence with four or fewer units accrues nine percent a year, charged monthly, with no penalty. Other property accrues twelve percent a year plus penalties of 3% on June 1 and 8% on December 1.

faqs.q: Can I pay Lincoln County property tax by phone?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer lists phone payment at 866-898-2915, along with online payment and mailed checks to PO Box 370, Davenport, WA 99122.
